concept.title: Conformability remains NP-complete for all fixed independence numbers at least 3
concept.concept_description: For every fixed integer k ≥ 3, the Conformability problem is NP-complete when restricted to connected d-regular graphs G of odd order n with independence number α(G) = k and maximum degree d ≥ n/2. The paper establishes this for k = 3 by reduction from perfect triangle packing in K₄-free graphs. The conjecture asserts that hardness persists for all larger independence numbers, where the complement graph has clique number k and conformable color classes correspond to cliques of odd size up to k in the complement, requiring richer packing structures to encode NP-hard problems.
concept.mathematical_framing: For every fixed integer k ≥ 3, the Conformability problem is NP-complete when restricted to connected d-regular graphs G of odd order n with independence number α(G) = k and maximum degree d ≥ n/2. The paper establishes this for k = 3 by reduction from perfect triangle packing in K₄-free graphs. The conjecture asserts that hardness persists for all larger independence numbers, where the complement graph has clique number k and conformable color classes correspond to cliques of odd size up to k in the complement, requiring richer packing structures to encode NP-hard problems.
concept.lean_guess: Adapt the paper's reduction by constructing, for each k ≥ 3, a family of connected d-regular graphs with α(G) = k and d ≥ n/2 whose conformability encodes exact clique-packing problems in K_{k+1}-free complements. For odd k, conformable color classes map to cliques of sizes 1,3,...,k in G̅; for even k, to cliques of sizes 1,3,...,k-1. The key challenge is designing gadgets that force the correct distribution of clique sizes in any conformable coloring, generalizing the triangle-packing enforcement at k=3. A reduction from exact cover by k-sets or k-clique packing in K_{k+1}-free graphs would establish hardness.

concept.title: Erdős Problem 550 for All Trees
concept.concept_description: The main theorem of the paper proves that for fixed integers k ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ m₁ ≤ … ≤ m_k, there exists n₀ = n₀(m₁,…,m_k) such that for every n ≥ n₀ and every n-vertex tree T, R(T, K_{m₁,…,m_k}) ≤ (k-1)(R(T, K_{m₁,m₂}) - 1) + m₁. We conjecture that the 'sufficiently large' condition can be removed entirely: the inequality holds for all trees T (i.e., for all n ≥ 1).
concept.mathematical_framing: The main theorem of the paper proves that for fixed integers k ≥ 2 and 1 ≤ m₁ ≤ … ≤ m_k, there exists n₀ = n₀(m₁,…,m_k) such that for every n ≥ n₀ and every n-vertex tree T, R(T, K_{m₁,…,m_k}) ≤ (k-1)(R(T, K_{m₁,m₂}) - 1) + m₁. We conjecture that the 'sufficiently large' condition can be removed entirely: the inequality holds for all trees T (i.e., for all n ≥ 1).
concept.lean_guess: Attempt to adapt the off-Turán embedding and compactness-rounding arguments to eliminate the dependence on n₀. Alternatively, perform a systematic case analysis for small n using structural properties of trees and known exact Ramsey numbers for small complete multipartite graphs.
